text.text_excerpt: I had an absolutely FANTASTIC time! Not gonna lie, we were a little nervous about going since more of our friends talked about the other escape room in the city, and when we got there, the post office building was a litttttttle sketchy. But once inside, it was fantastic. I can't remember the lady's name who was our host, but she was great. The room was fun, the story line was cute, and of course our group of friends was so competitive, and we got out of the room with 15 minutes to spare. Do yourself a favor and check this place out.

This was one of my favorite escape rooms. I have family in New Orleans so I visit often, and I came here with a friend of mine to try an escape game. When we arrived, we were already immersed in an interactive game. The decor is elaborate and beautiful, and we were offered to wear costumes during our adventure (I'm unsure if this is the case now due to COVID, but we had gone to this place pre-COVID). We played the jazz room, and there were endless puzzles and rooms to venture through. We almost made it to the end, and were so proud of ourselves for solving the majority of a tough game with just us two, but unfortunately, the final word got us stumped (this always seems to happen to me!). ...

I had a blast at Escape My Room tonight. My team of five and I did the Mardi Gras Study and successfully escaped with six minutes on the clock! I've done a couple other escape rooms at Clue Carre but much prefer Escape My Room. Walking up to the building, the entrance was kind of hidden in a sketchy alleyway but there are signs directing you where to go. Once inside, I was pleasantly surprised by the antique decor. I loved the way the rooms were furnished and found out they're actually based on the real DeLaporte mansion in New Orleans.
